title: Projective prime-to-ell log-smooth alteration over a trait
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$. A trait here is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a discrete valuation ring: a Noetherian local domain of dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal. A complete strictly henselian trait has $R$ complete for its maximal-ideal topology and henselian with separably closed residue field (henselian means that every simple root over the residue field of a monic polynomial over $R$ lifts to a root over $R$). Mixed characteristic means that $\operatorname{Frac}R$ has characteristic zero and the residue field has positive characteristic.

Use fs log structures, charts and log morphisms as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The canonical log structure on a trait is the subsheaf of $\mathcal O_S$ of sections invertible on its generic point; a uniformizer gives its chart $\mathbf N\to R$. In this statement, log smooth over that trait has its fs chart meaning: etale locally on source and target there are compatible charts $\mathbf N\to P$ with $P$ fine saturated, the group map injective with torsion in its cokernel of finite order invertible on the source, such that the induced scheme map to $S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[\mathbf N]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$ is smooth. Here $\mathbf Z[P]$ is the free abelian group on $P$ with multiplication induced by the monoid law.

Let $S$ be a complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $X$ be an integral regular scheme, flat and quasi-projective of finite type over $S$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Quasi-projective means that $X$ admits a locally closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^N_S$. There are a finite dominant extension of traits $T\to S$, an integral regular scheme $Y$ quasi-projective of finite type over $T$ and over $S$, an fs log structure $M_Y$ making $(Y,M_Y)\to T$ log smooth for the canonical trait log structure, and a projective dominant $S$-morphism $f:Y\to X$ that is generically finite etale of positive degree $d$ not divisible by $\ell$. Here projective means factoring as a closed immersion into $\mathbf P^m_X$ followed by projection, and generically finite etale means finite etale over a nonempty open of $X$, with $[k(Y):k(X)]=d$. No purity conclusion is included.

source.place: Expose XVI, section 3.7 second paragraph through its last paragraph, printed pp.254--255: semistable G-alteration, ell-Sylow H, tame equivariant modification, quotient over T=S prime/H, and log resolution. Geometric construction only, before applying Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7; preliminary finite extension to normalize constants in the first paragraph.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-trait-semistable-galois-alteration] to the given $X/S$. Obtain $G$, $S^{\prime}$, $a:X^{\prime}\to X$, and a nonempty open $U\subset X$ with $E=a^{-1}U\to U$ a connected finite etale $G$-torsor. Retain its $G$-stable divisorial fs log structure: $X^{\prime}$ is integral, regular, log regular, and log smooth over $S^{\prime}$. This input already includes normalization of the constants; we do not make an additional arbitrary-degree base change of $X$. Schemes finite type over the Noetherian traits are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian].

source.place: XVI 3.7, p.254, normalization of constants and the four bullets for the semistable G-alteration.

proof.text: Choose an $\ell$-Sylow subgroup $H\le G$ using [lem-weil-pbc-sylow-subgroup-prime-index]. Thus $\#H=\ell^r$ and $d=[G:H]>0$ is prime to $\ell$. Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}(\Gamma(S^{\prime},\mathcal O)^H)$. The order of $H$ is invertible on $S$, so [lem-per-tame-trait-quotient-log-etale] makes $T$ a complete strictly henselian trait finite dominant over $S$, and makes $X^{\prime}\to T$ log smooth. It is again of mixed characteristic: $\operatorname{Frac}((R^{\prime})^H)\subset\operatorname{Frac}R^{\prime}$ has characteristic zero, and the local inclusion $(R^{\prime})^H\subset R^{\prime}$ embeds the residue field of $T$ into that of $S^{\prime}$, of characteristic $p>0$. Only the degree of $S^{\prime}\to T$ divides $\#H$; the action on the trait need not be faithful.

source.place: XVI 3.7, p.254, the sentences choosing H and passing from S prime to T.

proof.text: The following explicit embeddings supply the quasi-projective hypotheses used below. Since $T\to S$ is finite, it is proper and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. The graph $X^{\prime}\to X^{\prime}\times_S T$ is a section of the separated projection, hence a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion]. Base-changing $X^{\prime}\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ and composing gives $X^{\prime}\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_T$. It is of finite type over $T$ by [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target]. More generally, in every composition below of a projective map $Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_B$ with an immersion $B\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_D$, base change gives an immersion $\mathbf P^m_B\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_D\times_D\mathbf P^n_D$, and the Segre embedding gives $Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{(m+1)(n+1)-1}_D$. These are just compositions of the cited immersions; [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft], [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e), and [lem-chow-segre] justify each arrow. In particular the resulting quasi-projectivity has the finite-projective-space meaning of the item.

source.place: XVI 3.7, p.254, quasi-projective models for the modifications and quotients; explicit graph and Segre bookkeeping.

proof.text: For every geometric point of $X^{\prime}$, its $H$-stabilizer has order dividing $\ell^r$. The residue characteristic is zero or the residue characteristic of $S$, different from $\ell$; the action is therefore tame. It is generically free since it is free on $E$. All hypotheses of [lem-per-gabber-log-smooth-equivariant-modification] now hold over $T$: integrality and log regularity come from Step 1, relative log smoothness from Step 2, and quasi-projectivity from Step 3. Obtain an $H$-equivariant projective birational $h:W\to X^{\prime}$ and the quotient $Q=W/H$ with its fs invariant log structure, log regular and log smooth over $T$. In particular $W$ is integral and quasi-projective of finite type over $T$.

source.place: XVI 3.7, p.254, tame action, equivariant modification X double-prime, and log-smooth quotient.

proof.text: The composite $W\xrightarrow h X^{\prime}\xrightarrow a X$ is projective by [lem-trf-h-projective-composition]. Apply [lem-per-projective-finite-group-quotient] with base $X$: $X$ is Noetherian and quasi-projective over the affine Noetherian $S$, and $W\to X$ is projective, hence quasi-projective. It gives a finite surjective quotient $q:W\to Q$, an integral $Q$, and a projective $v:Q\to X$. The categorical quotient is the same $Q$ as in Step 4 by the two universal properties. Applying the same theorem with base $T$ gives $Q/T$ quasi-projective of finite type. Step 3 makes $W/S$ quasi-projective from $h$ and $X^{\prime}/S$, so applying the quotient theorem with base $S$ gives $Q/S$ quasi-projective of finite type as well. These are the same scheme quotient and the induced structure maps, by uniqueness of categorical quotients.

source.place: XVI 3.7, p.254, quotient X double-prime/H and its morphism to X.

proof.text: Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$. It is a mixed-characteristic discrete valuation ring, so $\operatorname{Frac}A$ has characteristic zero. Apply the DVR clause of [lem-per-characteristic-zero-dedekind-excellent] to obtain excellence of $A$. This uses the characteristic-zero Dedekind theorem, not the excluded complete-local excellence interface. The integral fs log-regular $Q$, quasi-projective of finite type over $T$, now meets every hypothesis of [lem-per-log-regular-projective-log-resolution]. Obtain a projective birational saturated log-blowup tower $b:(Y,M_Y)\to Q$ with $Y$ integral and regular. That statement also says that the composite $Y\to Q\to T$ is log smooth. No purity assertion is invoked.

source.place: XVI 3.7, p.254, projective birational log resolution; excellence supplied by Stacks Tag 07QW(4).

proof.text: Set $f=v\circ b:Y\to X$. It is projective by [lem-trf-h-projective-composition]. Step 3 applied to $b$ and each of $Q/T$, $Q/S$ gives finite-projective-space immersions of $Y$ over both $T$ and $S$. Finite type follows from [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], since a projective embedding over a Noetherian base is finite type. All maps commute over $S$. To use proper images below, projective maps are proper: the projective-space projections are proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], closed immersions are proper and proper maps compose by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence].

source.place: XVI 3.7, pp.254--255, regular log-smooth X triple-prime and the projective morphism to X.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-birational-isomorphism-dense-open] to $h$. Its projectivity gives separatedness, and finite type over the Noetherian models gives local finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] on affines. Intersect the isomorphism open in $X^{\prime}$ with its finitely many $H$-translates. Inside the original torsor open, the complement has closed image under the finite $a$ and that image misses the generic point. Remove it and choose a nonempty affine subopen $U_1\subset U$. Then $W_{U_1}=X^{\prime}_{U_1}=E_1$ is the connected finite etale $G$-torsor. Quotient restriction in [lem-per-projective-finite-group-quotient] identifies $Q_{U_1}$ with its categorical $H$-quotient. Since $E_1$ is affine, its free $H$-action meets the affine-orbit hypothesis of [lem-sfb-admissible-free-finite-quotient]; that theorem identifies this same quotient with the fppf sheaf $E_1/H$.

source.place: XVI 3.7, p.255, generic degree of the quotient morphism; finite constant free quotient: Stacks 07S6 and fpqc descent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-admissible-free-finite-quotient] also to the $G$-action on the torsor $E=a^{-1}U$ itself. Its hypotheses hold: $E$ is open in $X^{\prime}$, which is quasi-projective over the affine $S$, hence separated; the action is free since it is simply transitive on geometric fibres of $E\to U$; and $E\to U$ is finite, hence affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], so the orbit of a point over $u\in U$ lies in the affine inverse image of an affine neighbourhood of $u$. The theorem's quotient is categorical, so by the Galois-cover definition [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois] and uniqueness of categorical quotients it is $U$, and its action-map clause gives $G\times E\cong E\times_UE$. Pulling back along the open $U_1\subset U$ gives $G\times E_1\cong E_1\times_{U_1}E_1$. Here is an explicit identification after this base change, rather than an assumption that arbitrary categorical quotients commute with it. In the fppf sheaf quotient description from Step 8, write a pair over $U_1$ uniquely as $(ge,e)$. Send its $H$-orbit to $(Hg,e)$. Conversely $(Hg,e)$ gives the class of $(ge,e)$; changing the representative $g$ changes only the $H$-orbit. These formulas are inverse on local sections and glue, so the representing schemes satisfy $Q_{U_1}\times_{U_1}E_1\cong(H\backslash G)\times E_1$. This has $d=[G:H]$ sheets over $E_1$. The cover $E_1\to U_1$ is fpqc by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: it is finite affine, surjective and flat, with flatness part of [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-finite] and [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-etale] to conclude that $Q_{U_1}\to U_1$ is finite etale. At the generic point set $K=k(U_1)$ and $L=k(E_1)$. The finite generic $K$-algebra $B$ satisfies $B\otimes_K L\cong L^d$. A $K$-basis of $B$ tensors to an $L$-basis, so $\dim_K B=d$.

source.place: XVI 3.7, p.255, generic degree of the quotient morphism; finite constant free quotient: Stacks 07S6 and fpqc descent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-birational-isomorphism-dense-open] to $b$, with local finite presentation checked on the same Noetherian affine charts as in Step 8. Obtain a dense open $V\subset Q$ over which $b$ is an isomorphism. The projective map $v$ is closed, so $v(Q\setminus V)$ is closed. It misses the generic point of $X$: Step 9 identifies the generic fibre of $Q/X$ with the spectrum of its function field, so its only point is the generic point of $Q$, which lies in $V$. Remove this closed image from $U_1$ to obtain a nonempty open $U_2$. Then $Y_{U_2}=Q_{U_2}$, so $f$ is finite etale of degree $d$ over $U_2$. Since $Y$ and $X$ are integral, its generic finite algebra is the field $k(Y)$, and its dimension over $k(X)$ is $d$: after the faithfully flat torsor extension in Step 9 it becomes $d$ copies of the base field. Hence $[k(Y):k(X)]=d>0$, $f$ is dominant, and $\ell\nmid d$ by Step 2. Together with Steps 6--7 this gives every clause of the item, without asserting punctual purity.

source.place: XVI 3.7, p.255, geometric conclusion preceding the purity application.
